note: A3.5. Deliberately legacy-only (no `cells`): the precision twin of angular-http-calls/client, which measures typescript/http_client. One Angular service with two OUTBOUND calls and no server anywhere. ts_routes' Shape-1 Express scan matched any `.get(`/`.post(` whose first argument is a `/` literal, so `this.http.get('/users')` also minted a server `route:/users` (ROUTE_METHOD `handler ""`, `file users.service.ts`, `line 0`), and HttpStackResolver then paired the service's own ENDPOINTs to that phantom: the graph reported a service calling itself over HTTP. A3.5 rejects `.get(`/`.post(` on an HTTP-client receiver (`http`, `*client`, `*api`, `dio` — code_domain::endpoint::is_http_client_receiver, shared with the Dart route scan). The ENDPOINTs and their CALLS edges must survive; only the phantom ROUTE and its pairings must die.
